task.task_name: Triage a personal auto collision claim
task.task_description: You handle new auto insurance claims. A policyholder reports a two-car collision at an intersection and sends in their account of what happened, vehicle details, damage photos, the other driver's contact and insurance information, and a police report number. Some details might be missing or conflicting, and there may not be a repair estimate yet. Your task is to check the claim against the policy and available records, see whether there's enough information to move it forward, flag missing documents or possible coverage issues, and send it to the right claims team. Straightforward claims can go through the usual process. Claims involving injuries, conflicting accounts, signs of possible fraud, or complicated coverage questions need specialist attention. You're getting the claim ready for an adjuster, who will make the final coverage and liability decisions.

operational_subtasks.subtask_name: Review and reconcile submitted claim facts
operational_subtasks.description: Review the policyholder’s account, vehicle and damage details, other-driver information, and any available police-report information; identify material inconsistencies or unclear facts.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: The supplied task describes several claim materials that may need comparison. Model estimate: one review per triaged claim, with moderate effort to cross-check the materials and resolve what is clear from the information provided.

operational_subtasks.subtask_name: Check policy and available records for coverage issues
operational_subtasks.description: Compare the reported loss and involved vehicle and insured details with the policy and available claim records; identify apparent mismatches or questions affecting coverage.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: The supplied task requires checking the claim against the policy and available records. Model estimate: one check per claim, with effort reflecting review of policy and record details and interpretation of any apparent discrepancy.

operational_subtasks.subtask_name: Assess claim information sufficiency and missing documents
operational_subtasks.description: Determine whether the available information is sufficient to move the claim forward; identify missing or needed documents or details, including whether a repair estimate or police report is needed for this claim.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Model estimate: one completeness assessment per claim, with additional review of possible gaps on some claims; the supplied task specifically notes that details may be missing and an estimate may not yet exist. The effort is limited to assessing and flagging gaps, not obtaining documents.

operational_subtasks.description: Evaluate whether the claim involves injury, conflicting accounts, indicators of possible fraud, or complicated coverage questions that warrant specialist attention rather than the usual claims process.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Model estimate: a screening on every claim, with more detailed consideration assumed for a minority of claims when a referral criterion appears present. The listed criteria come from the supplied task; their occurrence rates are not supplied.

operational_subtasks.subtask_name: Route the claim and communicate triage findings
operational_subtasks.description: Send the claim to the usual claims workflow or the appropriate specialist team, communicating to the receiving adjuster or team the triage basis, identified coverage concerns, and missing information or documents.
operational_subtasks.effort_rationale: Model estimate: one routing and handoff per claim. Effort covers selecting the destination and conveying a concise summary of findings and gaps; the supplied task requires sending the claim to the right team.

activities.expected_action: Check that the handoff is sufficiently supported by the available claim information, correct or request clarification of material errors, and make the final coverage and liability decisions.

activities.activity_name: Resolve or escalate unresolved claim exceptions
activities.description: A claims professional handles issues the automated triage cannot resolve, such as material conflicting facts, unanswered coverage questions, suspected fraud indicators, or information gaps that prevent the claim from moving forward.
activities.trigger: The agent identifies an unresolved material inconsistency, potential coverage issue, suspected fraud indicator, specialist-attention criterion, or information gap that requires human judgment or follow-up.
activities.expected_action: Determine the appropriate follow-up, request or obtain needed information, and escalate to the appropriate specialist or claims authority when warranted; update or redirect the handoff as needed.
